bss_slices.use: second registry lookup, once per flagged version node (phase 2b)

dispatch_guard.rule: on a first sight of a key, read the key vtable slot +0xd0; call it with (key, sink) unless it equals the identity function

log_dispatch.gate: vtable slot +0x40 of the sink object; returns without logging when level exceeds it
log_dispatch.signature: (level, &sink, format, file, varargs...); varargs are (file, r8, r9, ...)

malloc_branch.hook: 0x5f04ce0 with &dump-string; the binary's hook is a 5-byte no-op, so the string stays empty and the emits are unreachable as built
malloc_branch.rule: truncate the dump string, call the hook, emit only when the hook filled the string

not_claimed: what the virtual produce callee behind slot 0xe8 in the stats-emit routine computes
what the slot +0x38 produce callee or the slot +0xd0 dispatch callee compute
what the fields at +0x548, +0x360, +0x68, +0x700, +0x748, +0x17b4 or +0x4c1 denote beyond their offsets
the contents of the BSS slices at 0x65030e0 and 0x6502a80
why the head release runs twice when its marker differs
behaviour on a null owner object (the routine reads +0x17b4 unconditionally, so the model raises on a null object)

registry_lookup.return: matched node +0x28 slot, or 0 on a miss

skip_flag.rule: nonzero disposes the empty dump string and returns at once; no lock, no walk, no emit, no stats-emit call

thunk.semantics: loads *( *(rdi) ) into rdi and tail-jumps to the routine

trailing_bytes: bytes 0x5d7e627..0x5d7e630 are int3 padding, not part of the routine; the byte at 0x5d7e63f is int3 padding after the thunk

trim_invoke.target_rule: entry+0x08 when its low bit is clear; *( *(obj + entry+0x10) + entry+0x08 - 1 ) when set

version_release.old_1: full teardown via 0x5d8fef0, sized delete 0x9e8, returns 1
version_release.old_2: unlink +0x920/+0x930 pair, delete the +0x930 object, conditional free; returns 1 when it frees, 0 otherwise
version_release.rule: lock xadd -1 to the refcount at +0x38; the old value decides

walk.advance: release the old node when its marker differs from the sentinel, move to the +0x938 next node, bump the next refcount when its marker differs
walk.flag: node +0x3c; clear nodes are skipped without unlock or refresh
walk.head: *(*(*(object +0x68) +0x40) +0x110)
walk.head_release: on loop exit, release the head while its marker differs, re-tested after each call; at most two calls in the binary
walk.link: node +0x938, circular list headed by the head node
walk.per_node: unlock mutex; refresh(node+0x8d8, 0); when sink is non-null, produce via slot +0x38 on *(node+0x620) with the BlockCache string, insert the key into the hash table, dispatch slot +0xd0 on first sight; re-lock mutex
